issues.description: In the solution implementation of PersonResource.createPerson, the method returns HTTP 201 (ResponseEntity.status(201).build()) when the incoming Person already has an ID. This contradicts (a) the problem statement which requires rejecting creation requests that include an ID (i.e., treat them as invalid/new-person must not have an ID) and (b) the behavior of the analogous NoteResource.createNote which returns ResponseEntity.badRequest() when the Note has an ID. This divergence in response semantics is an unintentional inconsistency that can confuse students: they will look at NoteResource as the example and expect createPerson to behave similarly (return 400 Bad Request for invalid input).
issues.suggested_fix: Make PersonResource.createPerson reject incoming Person objects that already have an ID in the same way as NoteResource.createNote. Replace ResponseEntity.status(201).build() with ResponseEntity.badRequest().build(), and return the saved Person with a success status (e.g., ResponseEntity.ok(savedPerson)) when person.getId() is null. This aligns PersonResource semantics with the problem statement and the NoteResource example.
